records.name: Closed Core
records.definition: A core that cannot be extended without modifying its own source, so every addition edits the core.

records.name: Direct Control Ownership
records.definition: Application code driving the overall control flow itself instead of ceding it to a framework or container.

records.name: Direct Reference
records.definition: Referring to a specific implementation directly instead of looking it up through a registry.

records.name: Hardcoded Branch Constant
records.definition: Controlling a feature with a hardcoded constant in the code instead of an externally-managed flag.

records.name: Hardcoded Extensions
records.definition: Wiring extensions directly into the core so adding one requires editing and rebuilding the core.

records.name: Hardcoded Instantiation

distinctFrom.reason: Hardcoded instantiation constructs a dependency inside the class, while ambient context reads request or user state from an implicit global.

records.definition: Creating dependencies with hardcoded constructors inside a class instead of injecting them.

records.name: Hardcoded Lookup
records.definition: Hardcoding a service's address or instance instead of resolving it through a registry.

records.name: Continuous Delivery
records.definition: The ability to release changes to production continuously through an automated pipeline.

records.name: Decoupled Deploy and Release

distinctFrom.reason: Decoupling deploy from release separates shipping code from switching it on, while gradual rollout switches it on for a growing share of users.

records.definition: The ability to deploy code and separately decide when to activate it for users.

records.name: Dynamic Lookup
records.definition: The ability to find a registered component by key at runtime.

records.name: Dynamic Resolution
records.definition: The ability to resolve a service's current location or instance at runtime.

records.name: Framework Control Flow
records.definition: The ability to let a framework drive the overall control flow and call into application code.

records.name: Gradual Rollout
records.definition: The ability to enable a feature for a growing subset of users over time.

records.name: Late Resolution
records.definition: The ability to defer resolving which implementation to use until the moment it is needed.

records.name: Mocking
records.definition: The ability to substitute test doubles for real dependencies by injecting them.

records.name: Runtime Lookup
records.definition: The ability to look up a needed service by name at runtime.

records.name: Third-Party Extension
records.definition: The ability for outside developers to extend the system through published extension points.

records.name: Registry
records.definition: A central store that maps keys to registered components for later lookup.

records.name: Externalized Flag State
records.definition: The requirement that feature-flag values live in external configuration, not hardcoded in the code.

records.name: Keyed Registration
records.definition: The requirement that each component register under a unique key by which it can be retrieved.

records.name: Registration Protocol
records.definition: The requirement of a defined protocol by which services register and deregister themselves.

records.name: API Surface Growth
records.definition: The degree to which adding extension points enlarges the public API that must be kept stable.

records.name: Constructor Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which injecting many dependencies through constructors makes them long and unwieldy.

records.name: Explicit Dependencies

distinctFrom.reason: Explicit dependencies is the degree to which a component's needs are visible, while explicit dependency is the technique that makes them visible.

records.definition: The degree to which a component's dependencies are visible in its signature rather than acquired through hidden lookups.

records.name: Flag Debt
records.definition: The degree to which stale, unremoved feature flags accumulate and clutter the code over time.

records.name: Global State
records.definition: The degree to which a global registry behaves as shared global state that any code can reach.

records.name: Registry Availability
records.definition: The degree to which the whole system's operation depends on the service registry staying available.

records.name: Ungoverned Global Registry
records.definition: A defect in which a global registry is changed from anywhere, with no owner, lifecycle or validation of its entries.
